Notes: "C'est plutôt bien" = it's pretty good.
Swaps: bien · cher · calme

Notes: Understatement: it means mediocre or bad.
"T'inquiète !" on its own = no worries, I've got it.

Swaps: venir · t'excuser · insister
content · stressé · en forme

English: I'm tempted. / I'm up for it.
Notes: "Ça te tente ?" = Are you up for it?

English: There's nothing I can do about it.

Pattern: Ça ne sert à rien de + [infinitif]
Swaps: s'énerver · attendre · insister
réserver · partir tôt · ne rien dire

English: I struggle to… / I have trouble…
Swaps: comprendre · dormir · me lever

English: It doesn't ring a bell. / I don't feel like it.
Notes: Two meanings, context decides.
The opposite: "Ça tombe mal" (bad timing).

Literal: I have of it for five minutes.

Notes: In speech "évident" often means "easy".

French: Ça coûte les yeux de la tête.
English: It costs an arm and a leg.
Literal: It costs the eyes of the head.
Speak: Ça coûte les yeux de la tête.

Literal: He put a rabbit on me.

Notes: Short for "la grasse matinée".

English: I was miles away. / I was daydreaming.

Notes: Also disbelief: "Arrête, c'est pas vrai !"
Also signals you're leaving: "Allez, salut !"
Formal: "Allez-y !"

French: Ça te dirait de prendre un verre ?
English: Would you like to grab a drink?
Literal: Would that tell you to take a glass?
Swaps: dîner ensemble · venir · aller au cinéma
Speak: Ça te dirait de prendre un verre ?

French: Tu veux venir dîner à la maison ?
English: Do you want to come over for dinner?
Literal: You want to come dine at the house?
Speak: Tu veux venir dîner à la maison ?

Notes: Wine, flowers or dessert are safe gifts.
Means you're paying. Also "C'est moi qui invite."
Formal: "Faites comme chez vous."

English: Shall we greet with a kiss on the cheek?
Notes: The number of kisses depends on the region: usually two.

Literal: That goes to you very well.

French: Je suis là si tu as besoin.
English: I'm here if you need anything.
Literal: I am there if you have need.
Speak: Je suis là si tu as besoin.

Notes: Said all through January.

English: It was nice to see you.
I like you. / I'm attracted to you.
Notes: Romantic interest.
Real love only. "Je t'aime bien" = I like you (as a friend).

French: Je vois ce que tu veux dire, mais…
English: I see what you mean, but…
Speak: Je vois ce que tu veux dire, mais

French: Ce n'est pas ce que je voulais dire.
Literal: It's not what I wanted to say.
Speak: Ce n'est pas ce que je voulais dire.

English: That's got nothing to do with it.

Notes: Spoken French loves putting the topic up front.
Swaps: Le truc · L'idée · Le souci

French: Ce qui est bien, c'est que…
Speak: Ce qui est bien, c'est que

English: On one hand… on the other…
Literal: From one side… from the other…

English: As you like. / Up to you.

Notes: Can sound reluctant: "fine, if you insist".
